key_highlights: ASX slid to a three-month low as banks and miners fell amid oil price spikes, though earlier gains on easing crude were reversed intraday
AUD crushed after Fed failed 'Warshach test'; 10-year US Treasury yield topped 5%, pressuring global risk assets
Middle East oil shock risk elevated as Trump's conflict escalates, creating volatility for energy and transport sectors
IMF urges Australian government to cut spending ahead of another RBA rate hike; state interest costs soaring
Mining positives: record gold grades at Aguia (Colombia), Auric fast-tracks WA Burbanks plant, Barkly rare earth discovery in NT
Bathla collapse triggers insolvency storm; Cue and Veronika Maine fashion brands face collapse
Anthropic secures $31bn datacentre deal in western Queensland, signalling AI infrastructure buildout in Australia
Net overseas migration falls ahead of Labor migration cuts; real wages growth crushed by exploited workers

sectors.trend: Mixed: ASX miners fell on the day (contributing to 3-month low) but underlying fundamentals positive with record gold grades (Aguia), Burbanks plant acceleration (Auric), and Barkly rare earth discovery. Oil supply crunch at east-coast ports adds energy cost pressure.
sectors.implications: Gold and rare earths names (GOLD.AX, REE.AX, A2M.AX) benefit from discovery news. Iron ore/coal names (BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX) pressured by China demand uncertainty and oil-driven cost inflation. Fuel supply crunch (headline 36) raises input costs for miners.

sectors.trend: Banks fell sharply, contributing to ASX 3-month low. Citi's 11%+ RoTCE target signals global capital efficiency improvement, but BofA warns 10%+ drop in Q3 IB fees. Australian credit outpacing China's debt is a positive structural signal. State interest costs soaring pressures sovereign credit.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin pressure from rate uncertainty and sovereign credit stress. Private credit expansion (headline 37) poses systemic risk. IMF spending warnings add fiscal risk to bank loan books.

sectors.trend: Oil prices jumped again on Middle East conflict escalation, creating a supply shock narrative. East-coast fuel distributor supply crunch compounds domestic energy cost pressures. Green hydrogen spending questioned.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WLE.AX, SXG.AX benefit from oil spikes. However, fuel supply disruption raises input costs across transport and industrial sectors. Green hydrogen policy uncertainty (headline 54) weighs on renewable energy names.

sectors.trend: Severe stress: Cue and Veronika Maine face collapse; real wages growth crushed; jobseeker poverty rising. ACCC targeting real estate monopoly may shift consumer spending patterns. Tenants catching a break signals rental market softening.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WBC.AX (retail arms), and consumer discretionary names face headwinds. Housing/REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) may see rental yield compression. Fashion/retail collapse signals broader consumer confidence deterioration.

sectors.trend: Anthropic's $31bn Queensland datacentre deal signals major AI infrastructure investment. ASML scaling EUV tools for AI chip demand. Oracle adding $700m to AI transformation. Planted raises $31.8m for autonomous solar.
sectors.implications: Australian data/infrastructure plays (WTC.AX, SOL.AX, ASX-listed solar names) benefit from AI buildout. Long-term positive for Australian tech ecosystem but near-term capital expenditure heavy.

sectors.trend: BioNTech lung cancer breakthrough, Lilly's Foundayo gaining in oral weight-loss market, Novo Nordisk strategic reset. Iraqi-Australian type 1 diabetes research promising. Allied health cap scrapped for veterans.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX, and ASX-listed pharma/healthcare names benefit from global biotech momentum. Weight-loss drug competition (Lilly vs Novo) may pressure pricing but expands market.

key_themes: Fed rate decision and 10-year yield above 5% driving global risk-off; AUD under severe pressure
Middle East oil shock creating energy volatility and input cost inflation
Australian fiscal stress: IMF spending warnings, state interest costs, RBA hike looming
Consumer confidence deteriorating: fashion collapses, real wage stagnation, jobseeker poverty
Mining discovery pipeline positive (gold, rare earths, Burbanks) offsetting commodity price weakness
AI infrastructure investment accelerating in Australia (Anthropic $31bn deal)
Private credit and insolvency risk rising (Bathla collapse, rich-lister exposure)

risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge AUD exposure; favour domestic-revenue companies; monitor RBA response to 10-year yield spike
Overweight energy producers (WDS.AX, WLE.AX); underweight fuel-intensive transport and industrial names

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Australian fiscal deterioration / RBA rate hike
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce duration in fixed income; favour floating-rate REITs; monitor state bond spreads
Avoid overexposure to discretionary retail; monitor Cue/Veronika Maine contagion to other consumer names
Review exposure to leveraged private credit positions; favour investment-grade credit
Diversify mining exposure beyond iron ore; favour gold and rare earths hedges

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and rare earths miners on discovery pipeline and safe-haven demand
opportunities.rationale: Record gold grades, Burbanks acceleration, Barkly rare earths, and 10-year yield above 5% support precious metals and critical minerals

opportunities.recommendation: Add energy producers on Middle East oil shock and fuel supply crunch
opportunities.rationale: Oil jumping again; east-coast fuel distribution supply crunch supports domestic energy pricing power

opportunities.recommendation: Position in AI infrastructure and data centre beneficiaries
opportunities.rationale: Anthropic $31bn Queensland deal, ASML EUV scaling, Oracle AI spend signal multi-year Australian tech capex cycle

opportunities.recommendation: Selective healthcare exposure on global biotech momentum
opportunities.rationale: BioNTech lung cancer breakthrough, Lilly/Novo weight-loss competition expanding TAM; CSL benefits from global pharma strength

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce ASX 200 bank exposure; favour quality over yield
defensive_moves.rationale: Banks fell to 3-month low; RBA hike looming, state interest costs soaring, private credit risk rising, IMF spending warnings
Cue and Veronika Maine collapse, real wages crushed, jobseeker poverty rising signals prolonged consumer weakness

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge AUD/USD downside; favour AUD-earning domestic revenue streams
defensive_moves.rationale: AUD crushed on Fed failure; 10-year yield above 5% pressures AUD further; RBA may need to hike

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid leveraged private credit and high-yield positions
defensive_moves.rationale: Bathla insolvency storm, rich-lister private credit exposure, BofA IB fee decline signal credit cycle turning

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain volatile and under pressure. 3-month low on banks/miners, AUD weakness, and oil shock create headwinds. RBA rate hike expectations and IMF fiscal warnings add macro overhang. However, mining discovery news and energy pricing provide sector-specific support. Expect range-bound trading with downside bias into RBA decision.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive if oil shock resolves and RBA stabilises. AI infrastructure buildout (Anthropic, ASML) and mining discovery pipeline (gold, rare earths, Burbanks) offer structural growth. Consumer weakness and fiscal stress are the key drags. Superannuation reform debate (headline 41, 60) may reshape long-term capital flows.

Fed policy response to 10-year yield above 5%
Middle East oil supply resolution or escalation
Australian CPI and retail sales data
Bathla insolvency contagion to other sectors
IMF Article IV review recommendations implementation
watch_list: 10-year US Treasury yield (above 5%; key for global risk appetite)
Brent crude and Australian fuel supply (east-coast port congestion)
Iron ore and gold prices (China demand vs safe-haven bid)
RBA cash rate and forward guidance
State government bond spreads (soaring interest costs)
Consumer confidence and retail sales (Cue/Veronika Maine contagion)
